text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian Serb authorities are charging 30 German marks for enterance visas and 40 marks for transit visas to non-Bosnian pilgrims for Papal visit, says Moslem-Croat federation minister for communications, Rasim Gacanovic.
- Bosnian postal company begins installing 300 public telephone booths in the country. Some 100 should be installed in the capital Sarajevo.

- Only three candidates remain on the list for Sarajevo's mayor, Ismet Gavrankapetanovic, a county official from the ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA), says but declines to reveal their names.
- Sarajevo canton prime minister, Mustafa Mujezinovic, denies UNHCR allegation that Serbs and Croats were prevented from moving back to renovated flats in the city.

- A group of expelled Moslem inhabitants of north Bosnian village of Mahmutovici, which lies in Bosnian Serb entity, tries to enter village to plant seeds but Serb police turned them back with threats of force.
- Natural gas supplies for Sarajevo are cut due to Bosnian government's outstanding bill to a Russian gas company.

- Total number of missing persons from eastern Bosnian enclave of Srebrenica, which was overrun by Bosnian Serb army in July 1995, is 6,543, Bosnian war crimes institute in Tuzla says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
